plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Airy, daisy-like blooms float on slender stems above feathery, fern-like foliage. In mid-October they keep glowing in mild autumn gardens and sway in the breeze like paper lanterns. They carry on until the first hard frost ends the show.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer through autumn, continuing until the first frost
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere, such as the UK, northern Europe and the northern United States, where autumn frosts have not yet arrived by mid-October
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from the Greek word for order or harmony. It was named by Spanish priests in Mexico, the plant's homeland, who admired the tidy symmetry of its petals.
